inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent, fully diluted: Q2 2026 diluted weighted-average 3,253,335,432 ordinary shares / 10 ordinary shares per ADS = 325.334m ADS (6-K Q2-2026, EPS table). This already includes the shares issued on conversion of the 2026 convertible notes in H1 2026 (short-term debt fell 5,337 -> 911, APIC rose 9,653 -> 13,132). It is a quarter average, so it slightly overstates the period-end count after the RMB1,857m Q2 buyback. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.ads_ratio: 1 ADS = 10 ordinary shares; all per-share outputs are PER ADS in USD, comparable to the NASDAQ quote
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 (6-K Q2-2026 balance sheet, RMB m). Debt 7,219 = short-term debt 911 + long-term debt 3,315 + finance lease liabilities 62 + 2,931. Cash 15,706 = cash and equivalents 14,249 + restricted cash 142 + short-term investments 1,315. Operating lease liabilities (27,015) are NOT debt here: rent is expensed inside EBITDA under US GAAP ASC 842. Company-defined net cash is RMB10.2bn (excludes finance leases and short-term investments).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based compensation expenses, 20-F FY2025 cash flow statement and adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation (same figure). No separate equity-award tax-withholding line is disclosed in financing activities, so none is added. H1 2026 SBC ran at RMB265m (2.0% of revenue).
inputs.fx_note: CNY -> USD at 1/6.6712 = 0.1499 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-11-15). Parity check against the Hong Kong dual listing: 1179.HK HK$39.10 x 10 shares per ADS / 7.8455 (Yahoo HKD=X) = US$49.84 per ADS versus the NASDAQ close, a 1.1% tie (HK closed about 13 hours earlier), which confirms the ADS ratio and the quote basis. The 6-K's own convenience rate was 6.7851 at 30 June 2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government yield of roughly 1.8% plus an equity risk premium of roughly 7.5% including China country risk, beta about 1.0. The company holds net cash, so WACC is the cost of equity. The same rate is used in all three scenarios; China-macro, VIE and ADR-delisting risk is charged once, through the scenario flows and the raised bear weight, not through a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer (ASC 842). Operating lease rent (RMB1.0-1.1bn a quarter, the 'Rents' line) is an operating cost inside EBITDA and inside operating cash flow, so operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Finance leases (RMB2,993m) are not in EBITDA (they run through amortisation and interest), so their liability is included in debt. One treatment each, neither charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is small (RMB155m book; RMB6m of H1 2026 net income). The company's adjusted EBITDA starts from net income attributable to H World, so the flows are already attributable; the NCI stock is not deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (CNY flows against a USD ADS quote, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule). Reason: H World is an operating company, a hotel franchisor/operator whose value is a stream of free cash flow; it is not a REIT (it leases rather than owns its hotels and earns half its revenue from franchise fees). First valuation of this ticker, no prior DCF. EBITDA margin paths are on the company's adjusted-EBITDA basis (before SBC, FX and fair-value items; FY2025 8,473 = 33.5%, trailing twelve months to June 2026 9,290 = 34.9%), not the core_metrics EBITDA, which is operating income plus D&A after SBC. Interest income is stripped from the flows because net cash exceeds one year of FCF. Buybacks: a real repurchaser (RMB783m FY2025, RMB1,857m in H1 2026, and a new US$2.5bn three-year return plan), so the flat share count is being funded. Not captured: any buybacks after 30 June 2026 and Q3 2026 results, which had not been filed at the valuation date.

equity_bridge.note: 6-K Q2-2026 balance sheet. Equity-method and equity-security holdings; their income is outside adjusted EBITDA margin paths, so the asset goes in the bridge (matching-asset rule).
US$275m (US$0.87 per ADS) declared 17 Aug 2026, record date 8 Sep 2026, paid after the 30 June balance sheet; converted at about 6.70. The quote is ex-dividend, so the cash is removed.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 guidance (Group revenue +4% to +8%) and the fee-revenue mix shift; the trailing CAGRs are not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (2.5%) diverges from revenue 5-year CAGR (19.9%) by far more than 30%. Neither is a usable growth anchor: FY2020 and FY2022 are COVID-depressed bases (FY2020 and FY2022 EPS were negative, so EPS CAGRs are undefined), and equity is held down by RMB3.5-3.9bn a year of dividends plus buybacks.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2022 337, FY2023 6,382, FY2024 6,088, FY2025 6,898. The 3-year FCF CAGR off the FY2022 lockdown base is meaningless; FY2023 to FY2025 is +4.0% a year. EPS FY2019 0.59 to FY2025 1.60 per ordinary share is 18% a year over six years (FY2018 and earlier are on the pre-split share basis and are excluded). SBC rose from 0.65% of revenue in FY2023 to 1.66% in FY2025 and 2.0% in H1 2026, so owner FCF has grown slower than reported FCF.

base.rationale: Year 1 is FY2026: guidance is +4% to +8% and H1 2026 came in at +11.0%, so 7.5% sits near the top of the range. Margin starts at 35.5% against 34.9% trailing and rises 3.5 points over ten years as manachised/franchised fees pass 50% of revenue. Cash tax 29% matches the FY2025 effective rate of 29.6% (25% statutory plus dividend withholding tax); cash tax actually paid in FY2025 was lower (RMB1,632m against a RMB2,161m expense), so this is not flattered by timing. D&A converges on capex. Working-capital capture of 10% reflects upfront franchise fees and loyalty deferred revenue (deferred revenue rose RMB252m on RMB1,416m of revenue growth in FY2025, 18%).

scenario_narratives.base: The network keeps growing at roughly 2,200 gross openings and 600-700 closures a year, but same-hotel RevPAR stays flat to slightly down (it was -3.0% in Q2 2026) as China's budget and midscale supply is absorbed slowly. Revenue grows 7.5% in FY2026, then slows from 6% to 3% as leased-and-owned revenue shrinks and fee revenue (16-20% growth in FY2026) becomes the larger half. Adjusted EBITDA margin rises from 35.5% to 39% on that mix shift. H World International stays a low-margin, roughly break-even contributor.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chinese hotel supply growth fades after the 2023-2025 glut and RevPAR turns positive, while the brand-mix upgrade (Grand JI, Crystal Orange 2.5, upper-midscale conversions) lifts ADR. The 3,000-plus pipeline converts on schedule, franchisees keep signing because H Rewards (300m-plus members, about 73% of room nights) fills rooms more cheaply than online travel agents, and leased-hotel exits in China and Germany accelerate the fee mix. Revenue grows 7-8.5% for five years and margin reaches 43%, still well below pure-franchise global peers because a leased estate remains.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese consumer and business travel weaken and oversupply persists; RevPAR falls several percent a year for two to three years while Atour, Jinjiang and BTG compete for the same franchisees. Because leased-hotel rent is fixed (about RMB4bn a year), falling RevPAR hits margin hard: adjusted EBITDA margin drops from 34.5% to 31.5% and only partly recovers. Franchisee returns deteriorate, openings slow and closures rise, so revenue growth stalls at 1-2.5%. A US-China delisting or VIE shock would add a valuation discount on top that this cash-flow path does not model.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: about 83% of revenue depends on mainland China travel demand, same-hotel RevPAR is already falling, and the ADR carries VIE and delisting risk that sits outside the flows. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice in 2026 and the fee-mix shift is visible in reported margins. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs both a RevPAR recovery and continued franchisee demand, which depend on the same Chinese consumer cycle but are not yet evidenced in same-hotel data.

valuation_philosophy.summary: H World is valued as a cash-generating hotel franchisor with a shrinking leased estate. Owner FCF is built from adjusted EBITDA less SBC, tax at the full effective rate, and capex, in CNY at a CNY-built 9.5% discount rate, then converted to USD per ADS. Net cash, long-term investments and the dividend paid since the balance sheet date are bridged separately. China and ADR risk is carried in the scenario weights, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Same-hotel RevPAR in China: fixed leased-hotel rent means each point of RevPAR moves margin disproportionately
Franchisee economics: the pipeline and fee growth depend on third-party owners continuing to earn acceptable returns
Tax leakage: 10% PRC dividend withholding on cash upstreamed to fund the US$2.5bn return plan could push the cash rate above 29%
FX: flows are CNY, the quote is USD; the value per ADS moves one-for-one with USD/CNY
VIE structure and US delisting risk, which no cash-flow path captures
The balance sheet is 30 June 2026; Q3 2026 results and post-June buybacks are not yet reflected
